events.continuity_hook: Only the outbound timing conflicts with the new crate delivery; the three-night lodging and Thursday evening flight remain aligned with the work schedule.

events.continuity_hook: The Sunday ceremony fixes the central commitment, but the best flight pairing and hotel area remain open while the Saturday family gathering affects location convenience.

events.continuity_hook: The later outbound constraint narrows the flight choices and may remove Friday's hotel night, but the family events and Monday return have not moved.

events.interaction_goal: Verify that the hotel has joined the consecutive reservations, confirm the complete three-night total and Thursday checkout, and review the final museum-to-airport schedule against the ticketed departure.

events.continuity_hook: The weekend and main family commitment are established, but transportation, Sunday timing, and the shared lodging remain open.

events.continuity_hook: The later installation finish resolves the return day and lodging dates, while the exact flights and hotel remain unbooked.

events.continuity_hook: The weekend and purpose are established, while the travel mode, arrival time, Sunday return, and two-night hotel remain unchosen.
events.interaction_goal: Compare realistic door-to-door timing for flying and driving, identify workable Friday and Sunday schedules, and establish the area and dates for a shared hotel stay.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife plan a Friday-to-Sunday visit to relatives in Raleigh and will share one hotel room. They need to arrive before a Saturday morning family gathering, but Friday work obligations make both an evening flight and a drive after work plausible; Sunday departure timing remains open around a late lunch.

events.continuity_hook: The travel mode and two-night stay are now fixed, while the hotel location and rate remain open.
events.interaction_goal: Compare available hotels convenient to the family gathering, confirm late Friday check-in and complete two-night charges, and choose a cancellable room for two adults.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife determine that driving after work on Friday is more practical than flying once airport time and transportation for two people are included. They can leave Atlanta around 5:30 p.m., expect a late arrival in Raleigh, and plan to drive home after Sunday’s late family lunch; a shared hotel room for Friday and Saturday nights is still unbooked.

events.continuity_hook: Driving times are settled, and the full hotel costs and cancellation terms can now determine the lodging choice.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate the comparable two-night totals, account for Saturday and Sunday driving, and reserve one room for Avery and her wife.
events.scenario_brief: Two Raleigh hotels remain under consideration for the shared Friday-to-Sunday stay. The lower-priced option is farther from Saturday’s gathering and charges for parking, while the closer property has a higher room rate but includes parking and permits cancellation until Thursday evening; both accept late arrival.

events.continuity_hook: The room is booked, but changed parking arrangements affect the cost and convenience of arriving late Friday.
events.interaction_goal: Verify overnight access and the revised parking total, compare it with the alternate hotel’s current total, and decide whether to keep or replace the reservation before the deadline.
events.scenario_brief: The reserved Raleigh hotel sends a notice that its parking deck will be closed during the weekend, with guest parking moved to a public garage two blocks away at a different daily charge. Avery’s cancellation window remains open until the following evening, and the previously compared hotel still has a room available.

events.continuity_hook: A new work assignment has fixed the Sunday arrival and Monday start, while the possible Thursday inspection prevents finalizing the return and lodging span.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Sunday outbound flights, identify viable Wednesday evening and Thursday return options, and establish hotel dates that can accommodate the unresolved inspection.
events.scenario_brief: Avery is assigned to supervise the installation of a traveling exhibition in New Orleans from Monday through Wednesday. She must be at the museum by 8:00 a.m. Monday, installation is expected to end near 4:00 p.m. Wednesday, and a Thursday morning contingency inspection may be added after the first day; Sunday travel is therefore necessary, but the return day and hotel checkout remain uncertain.

events.continuity_hook: The Thursday obligation fixes a four-night stay and eliminates the Wednesday return, but the exact flights have not been selected.
events.interaction_goal: Select and book a practical Sunday outbound and Thursday afternoon return, including adequate ground-travel margins at both ends.
events.scenario_brief: The host museum confirms that the contingency inspection will occur at 9:00 a.m. Thursday and should finish by noon. Avery now needs a Sunday flight that leaves enough time to reach the hotel before an early Monday start and a Thursday return that allows realistic travel from the museum to the airport after the inspection.

events.continuity_hook: Flight times and the four-night lodging span are fixed, so total cost, daily access to the museum, and rate terms remain to be resolved.
events.interaction_goal: Compare complete four-night totals and morning travel times, verify Thursday luggage handling, and reserve the hotel that best fits the work schedule.
events.scenario_brief: Avery’s Sunday outbound and Thursday return are booked, leaving four hotel nights to arrange. One available hotel is within walking distance of the museum but requires full payment several days before arrival, while another is a short streetcar ride away, has a lower room charge, and adds a nightly destination fee; both can hold luggage after Thursday checkout.

events.continuity_hook: The hotel choice is settled, but the reservation currently ends one night too early for the fixed work schedule and return flight.
events.interaction_goal: Extend the existing reservation through Thursday checkout, retain the quoted nightly terms if available, and obtain a corrected four-night confirmation.
events.scenario_brief: After Avery reserves the walkable New Orleans hotel, the confirmation shows checkout on Wednesday even though her booked return flight leaves Thursday afternoon and the Thursday morning inspection requires a fourth night. The property still shows the same room available for Wednesday night, but the confirmation must be corrected before the advance-payment date.

events.continuity_hook: The vacation dates and shared-room arrangement are established, while the destination, driving schedule, and lodging area remain open.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the three coastal destinations using realistic driving times and current six-night lodging availability, then narrow the trip to one island and a practical arrival plan.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife begin planning a six-night September coastal vacation from Saturday through Friday. Amelia Island, Jekyll Island, and Tybee Island are all reachable by car from Atlanta, but they differ in drive time, the concentration of hotels directly by the ocean, and the availability of rooms with private balconies for the full stay.

events.continuity_hook: The destination, dates, and travel mode are fixed, leaving the exact beachfront area and hotel shortlist to determine.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm which hotels provide direct beach access, distinguish private ocean-view balconies from generic balcony listings, and create a shortlist with complete six-night costs.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife choose Amelia Island and plan to drive from Atlanta on Saturday morning. Several properties have rooms for all six nights, but some are across a main road from the beach, while two oceanfront options list balcony rooms with different view descriptions, parking charges, and cancellation dates.

events.continuity_hook: Avery has a focused oceanfront shortlist, but the quoted totals are not directly comparable because the included items, fees, deposits, and cancellation terms differ.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate comparable totals for one room and two adults, separate refundable deposits from actual charges, verify the balcony categories, and identify the stronger booking option.
events.scenario_brief: Two Amelia Island hotels remain viable for the six-night stay. One offers a higher-floor partial-ocean-view balcony and includes breakfast but adds nightly parking; the other has a lower total room charge and a direct-ocean-view balcony but adds a resort fee and requires a larger deposit. Their cancellation deadlines fall on different days.

events.continuity_hook: The leading rate no longer provides one room category for the whole vacation, forcing a choice between moving rooms mid-stay and paying more for an uninterrupted stay.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the split-room arrangement with the continuous six-night option, confirm whether the property handles luggage during the room move, and decide which stay to book.
events.scenario_brief: Before Avery books, the direct-ocean-view room at the lower-priced hotel becomes unavailable for the first two nights. That property can offer a standard room followed by an in-stay move to the balcony room, while the other shortlisted hotel still has its partial-ocean-view balcony category for all six nights at the earlier quote.

events.continuity_hook: The hotel and room category are selected; booking details and the road-trip arrival estimate are the remaining administrative steps.
events.interaction_goal: Reserve the selected room for both travelers, record a realistic arrival window, verify the complete charge and cancellation deadline, and produce the confirmed drive-and-hotel itinerary.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife choose the uninterrupted six-night balcony stay and are ready to reserve it. Their planned Saturday drive should reach Amelia Island in midafternoon, but the rate requires arrival by 6:00 p.m. unless the hotel records a later arrival, and the final confirmation must include both adults, parking, and the Friday checkout date.

events.continuity_hook: The uninterrupted balcony reservation is confirmed, but temporary loss of direct beach access reopens the hotel decision shortly before its cancellation deadline.
events.interaction_goal: Verify the walkway closure dates and shuttle hours, compare the current all-in cost and cancellation terms of the available oceanfront room, and decide whether to retain or replace the existing reservation.
events.scenario_brief: The Amelia Island hotel advises Avery that its main beach walkway will be closed for repairs during the first three days of the six-night stay. The balcony room, parking arrangement, and Friday checkout remain unchanged, but guests would need to use a public access point reached by a hotel shuttle. Cancellation is still available until the following afternoon, and the other shortlisted oceanfront property now has one direct-ocean-view room available for all six nights at a higher current total.

events.continuity_hook: A new museum assignment establishes the destination and Tuesday start while leaving the return and lodging span dependent on a possible Thursday review.
events.interaction_goal: Compare practical Monday flights from Atlanta, identify viable Wednesday evening and Thursday afternoon returns, and outline lodging dates that can accommodate either work schedule.
events.scenario_brief: Avery is assigned to oversee the receipt and unpacking of an exhibition in St. Louis. She must report to the museum at 8:00 a.m. Tuesday, installation is scheduled through 6:00 p.m. Wednesday, and a Thursday condition review may be required depending on what is found during unpacking. Monday travel is necessary, but the return day and hotel checkout cannot yet be fixed.

events.continuity_hook: The Thursday review removes the Wednesday return option and fixes the flight window, while the exact itinerary remains unbooked.
events.interaction_goal: Compare available round trips, confirm that the Thursday departures allow adequate ground-travel time after the review, and book the outbound and return itinerary.
events.scenario_brief: The receiving museum confirms that Avery must attend the Thursday condition review from 9:30 a.m. until about 1:00 p.m. She now needs a Monday outbound that leaves enough time to reach the hotel and prepare for Tuesday morning, plus a Thursday return with a realistic margin for travel from the museum to the airport.

events.continuity_hook: The flight dates now fix a Monday-through-Thursday stay, leaving total lodging cost, morning access to the museum, and rate terms to resolve.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate complete three-night totals, compare realistic Tuesday morning travel times, verify luggage storage after Thursday checkout, and reserve the property that best fits the assignment.
events.scenario_brief: With Monday and Thursday flights booked, Avery needs three hotel nights. A property near the museum permits a short walk to the Tuesday start but charges separately for breakfast, while a less expensive hotel near a light-rail stop requires a transfer on the first morning. Both have Thursday luggage storage, but only one rate can be canceled through the weekend before arrival.

events.continuity_hook: The original outbound no longer provides the planned Monday arrival, while the Thursday return and three-night hotel reservation remain usable.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the airline's no-cost rebooking options, compare the remaining earlier departures and baggage charges, and replace only the Monday outbound without disturbing the Thursday return.
events.scenario_brief: The airline moves Avery's booked Monday flight to an evening departure that would reach St. Louis after 9:00 p.m., substantially reducing preparation time before the 8:00 a.m. museum start. An earlier flight on the same airline and an afternoon flight on another carrier still have seats, but their rebooking costs and baggage terms differ.

events.continuity_hook: An on-site finding extends the assignment by one day, requiring coordinated changes to both the return flight and hotel while Avery is already traveling.
events.interaction_goal: Move the return to a practical Friday departure after the second check, add Thursday night without forcing a room move, and reconcile the updated flight and hotel confirmations into one itinerary.
events.scenario_brief: During Thursday's condition review, the museum finds a crate reading that requires Avery to remain for a second check at 10:00 a.m. Friday. Her return flight is booked for Thursday afternoon and her hotel reservation ends Thursday morning; the hotel can keep her in the same room for one additional night, but only under a separately priced reservation.

events.continuity_hook: The extra night and Friday return have been arranged, but conflicting itinerary displays and the separate hotel record need to be reconciled before departure.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm that the Friday flight is ticketed, verify that the Thursday segment no longer requires action, link the added hotel night to the same room, and arrange checkout and luggage handling around the museum visit.
events.scenario_brief: After the Thursday extension was arranged, Avery receives a Friday flight confirmation but the airline app still displays the canceled Thursday segment, and the hotel's added night appears under a separate confirmation number. She must leave for the 10:00 a.m. museum check before hotel checkout and expects to travel directly to the airport afterward.

events.continuity_hook: A new museum assignment fixes the Monday outbound and Tuesday start but leaves Wednesday departure timing dependent on the packing schedule.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Monday flights that allow an orderly evening arrival, identify Wednesday night and Thursday morning return options, and outline a lodging span that can accommodate either release time.
events.scenario_brief: Avery is assigned to inspect and document a group of objects in Denver before they are packed for an Atlanta exhibition. She must be at the collection facility by 9:00 a.m. Tuesday, work continues through Wednesday, and the packing supervisor cannot yet guarantee whether she will be released at 3:30 p.m. or closer to 6:00 p.m. Wednesday. Monday travel is fixed, while the return and hotel checkout strategy remain open.

events.continuity_hook: The Wednesday release time narrows the return choices enough to book a round trip, with airport transfer time and baggage cost still to compare.
events.interaction_goal: Select a Monday outbound and realistic Wednesday return, calculate the fare with one checked equipment bag, and complete the round-trip booking.
events.scenario_brief: The packing supervisor now commits to releasing Avery by 4:00 p.m. Wednesday. Two evening nonstop returns remain viable, but the earlier one leaves little margin for the trip from the collection facility to the airport, while the later one arrives in Atlanta near midnight. Several Monday afternoon outbound choices are also available with different checked-bag charges.

events.continuity_hook: The flight itinerary fixes a two-night stay, leaving location, complete cost, and rate terms to resolve.
events.interaction_goal: Compare complete two-night charges and realistic Tuesday travel times, verify early luggage storage, and reserve the hotel and rate that fit the work schedule.
events.scenario_brief: With Monday and Wednesday flights booked, Avery needs two hotel nights. One property is a short ride from the collection facility and offers early luggage storage on Tuesday, while another is less expensive and near the airport rail line but would require a longer rideshare trip for the 9:00 a.m. start. The lowest rate at the closer hotel must be prepaid, while a higher rate remains cancelable until shortly before arrival.

events.continuity_hook: The canceled outbound threatens preparation for Tuesday's inspection, while the rest of the booked trip should remain intact.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the replacement itineraries, account for the checked equipment bag and connection risk, rebook only Monday's travel, and notify the hotel of the resulting arrival time.
events.scenario_brief: The day before departure, Avery's Monday outbound is canceled because of an aircraft issue. The airline offers a no-cost evening flight that would reach Denver after 10:00 p.m.; an earlier routing through another city is available but has a short connection, and a different carrier has a nonstop seat at an added cost. Her Wednesday return and two-night hotel booking are still valid.

events.continuity_hook: The wedding dates, two travelers, and driving plan are fixed, but the hotel, room type, and Friday arrival timing have not been settled.
events.interaction_goal: Compare complete two-night hotel costs, confirm room availability for both adults, check practical travel time to the wedding events, and create a shortlist with cancellation deadlines.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife plan to drive from Atlanta to Nashville for a Saturday family wedding and need one room for Friday and Saturday nights. The ceremony hotel has limited inventory because another large event is nearby, while two hotels within a short rideshare trip still show rooms with either one king bed or two queens. The family dinner begins Friday at 7:00 p.m., so they need to arrive in time to check in and change.

events.continuity_hook: The earlier shortlist is ready for a decision, with room type, full two-night cost, and refund terms now clear.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the final totals and transportation implications, verify one king room for two adults, and reserve the better fit for Friday and Saturday nights.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife have narrowed the Nashville wedding stay to the ceremony hotel and a nearby property with king rooms still available. The ceremony hotel costs more but avoids rideshares after the reception, while the nearby hotel has a refundable rate and confirms that a Friday arrival before the 7:00 p.m. family dinner is practical.

events.continuity_hook: The room remains confirmed, while the temporary garage closure introduces a last-mile issue for check-in and the Friday dinner.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm nearby overnight parking, determine whether luggage can be dropped before parking, and record the check-in plan without replacing the hotel reservation.
events.scenario_brief: Several days before the drive, the reserved Nashville hotel reports that its garage will be unavailable Friday evening. Avery and her wife still expect to reach the city shortly before hotel check-in, and the family dinner venue has not changed, but they now need a workable place to leave the car without delaying their arrival.

events.continuity_hook: The travel week and road-trip format are established, but the destination and lodging budget remain open.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the two coastal areas for drive time, beach access, and representative six-night hotel totals, then choose one area for a focused property search.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife begin planning a six-night late-summer coastal trip within driving distance of Atlanta. They are comparing Amelia Island and the South Carolina coast, want straightforward walking access to the ocean, and have not yet decided whether a beachfront room is worth the higher total once resort and parking charges are included.

events.continuity_hook: The destination is fixed, allowing the search to move from regional comparison to complete lodging costs and actual walking routes to the beach.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate comparable six-night totals, verify the walking route and beach entrance for each property, and reduce the options to two hotels with suitable refund terms.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife choose Amelia Island and are considering three hotels for the six-night stay. One is directly on the beach with costly parking, one is across a low-traffic road from a public beach entrance, and one is several blocks inland but includes breakfast; advertised nightly rates do not include all taxes and property fees.

events.continuity_hook: Complete hotel totals and beach routes have already been compared, leaving room outlook, balcony details, and rate timing to settle before booking.
events.interaction_goal: Verify the balcony and view descriptions for the available king rooms, compare final totals and refund dates, and book one room for both travelers for all six nights.
events.scenario_brief: The two remaining Amelia Island hotels both have rooms for the selected week. The beachfront property offers either a standard king room facing inland or a more expensive ocean-view king with a small balcony, while the hotel across the road offers a larger balcony room but only a partial ocean view; one quoted rate becomes nonrefundable sooner than the other.

events.continuity_hook: The six-night reservation is active, but the room category and practical beach route need confirmation before the rate loses flexibility.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the exact balcony room category in writing, determine which beach entrance will be available, and decide whether the existing reservation still matches the trip before its refund deadline.
events.scenario_brief: Two weeks before the Amelia Island drive, Avery reviews the reservation and finds that the confirmation lists a king room but does not state the booked balcony category. The hotel has also posted a temporary notice about work near one beach access path, making it unclear whether the usual short route to the ocean will be open during their stay.

events.continuity_hook: The room category and alternate ocean route are now documented, allowing a final decision on the active reservation before its refund deadline.
events.interaction_goal: Review the confirmed room and walking route, retain or cancel the reservation before the deadline, and record the final six-night lodging details.
events.scenario_brief: The Amelia Island hotel confirms in writing that Avery and her wife hold the larger balcony king room for all six nights. The access path beside the property will be closed during daytime construction, but a public entrance about a six-minute walk away will remain open throughout their stay; the refundable rate expires that evening.

events.continuity_hook: The work dates establish the outbound window, while the unresolved Thursday release time leaves the return leg open.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Sunday evening and Monday morning outbound flights, identify realistic Thursday return choices, and hold a workable itinerary until the lender confirms the handoff schedule.
events.scenario_brief: Avery is assigned to oversee an exhibition installation in Chicago. The cases are scheduled to reach the museum Monday afternoon, installation occupies Tuesday and Wednesday, and a lender handoff is tentatively planned for Thursday morning. She needs to travel from Atlanta on Sunday or early Monday, but the handoff end time is not yet firm enough to choose a Thursday return.

events.continuity_hook: The release time and baggage arrangement resolve the two uncertainties that prevented the round trip from being selected.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the Sunday outbound and a Thursday return with enough time to reach the airport after the handoff, confirm the fare for one traveler, and book the round trip.
events.scenario_brief: The lender confirms that Avery should be free by 1:00 p.m. Thursday, and the equipment crate will ship separately rather than travel as checked baggage. The previously identified Sunday evening outbound remains available, along with two Thursday nonstop returns that differ in airport waiting time and Atlanta arrival time.

events.continuity_hook: The flight times fix the stay length and Sunday arrival, leaving total cost, Monday access, and rate terms to settle.
events.interaction_goal: Compare complete four-night charges and Monday travel times, verify late check-in, and reserve the property and rate that fit the installation schedule.
events.scenario_brief: With the flights booked, Avery needs four hotel nights from Sunday through Thursday. A hotel within walking distance of the museum has a higher total and can accept a late arrival, while a less expensive property near a rail stop requires a transfer and a longer trip to the loading dock for Monday's case delivery. Their cancellation deadlines also differ.

events.continuity_hook: The delayed shipment extends the booked work trip by one day without changing the outbound journey.
events.interaction_goal: Move only the return flight to Friday with adequate airport transfer time, compare the resulting fare difference, extend the hotel through Friday checkout, and verify both updated confirmations.
events.scenario_brief: Three days before departure, the Chicago museum reports that a dock problem has delayed the cases until Tuesday morning, pushing final installation work and the lender handoff to Friday noon. Avery's Sunday outbound remains useful, but the Thursday return and four-night hotel stay now end too early; Friday nonstop seats and one additional night at the same hotel are still available.

events.continuity_hook: The family event and two-traveler weekend window are fixed, opening a new trip whose flight timing must be settled before lodging is chosen.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the Friday and Sunday nonstop combinations for two adults, account for the practical arrival margin, and choose a flight pair to carry into booking.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife plan to attend her father-in-law's Saturday evening retirement dinner in Milwaukee. They can leave Atlanta after work on Friday and return Sunday, but an early Friday nonstop would require taking part of the day off, while the later nonstop arrives with little margin if delayed. Sunday options include an afternoon departure and a less expensive evening flight.

events.continuity_hook: The prior comparison established the viable nonstop combinations; the travelers have now chosen the timing tradeoff and are ready to purchase.
events.interaction_goal: Verify the dates, passenger count, fare conditions, and total for the selected Friday outbound and Sunday evening return, then book the round trip for both travelers.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife decide that protecting their arrival before Saturday evening's retirement dinner matters more than avoiding a partial Friday absence from work. The earlier Friday nonstop and the less expensive Sunday evening return are still available for two adults, but the fare conditions and combined total need to be checked before purchase.

events.continuity_hook: The booked flight schedule fixes Friday arrival and Sunday departure, allowing lodging to be compared for the exact two-night stay.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the full two-night cost, parking charges, cancellation terms, and travel time to the dinner venue, then reserve one room for both travelers.
events.scenario_brief: With the Milwaukee flights confirmed, Avery and her wife need two nights near the retirement dinner venue. Her father-in-law's suggested hotel has a family room block that may close soon, while a nearby independent hotel quotes a lower base rate but adds overnight parking; neither complete two-night total has been established.

events.continuity_hook: Both the round trip and hotel are booked, but the schedule change creates a late-arrival issue that must be resolved across the two reservations.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the revised nonstop with the offered connection, confirm whether the hotel can hold the room for the later arrival, and either accept the new flight time or change the outbound while leaving the Sunday return intact.
events.scenario_brief: Five days before the Milwaukee visit, the airline moves Avery and her wife's Friday flight later by nearly two hours. The revised arrival still permits the family dinner the next evening, but it falls after the hotel's stated check-in desk hours, and the airline offers either acceptance of the change or a no-fee move to an earlier connecting itinerary.

events.continuity_hook: This begins a new work episode with three fixed cities and two firm meetings, while the middle flight cannot yet be selected confidently.
events.interaction_goal: Map feasible Atlanta-to-Washington, Washington-to-Boston, and Boston-to-Atlanta flights, identify which middle options depend on the release time, and retain a workable itinerary for confirmation.
events.scenario_brief: Avery is assigned to accompany a small traveling exhibition through two institutional handoffs. She must be in Washington, D.C., for a Tuesday morning condition review, continue to Boston after a Wednesday afternoon release, and return to Atlanta after a Friday morning receiving meeting; the precise Wednesday release window is the only unresolved schedule point.

events.continuity_hook: The release time and separate shipment resolve the uncertainties that kept the three-city itinerary from being purchased.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the middle leg with sufficient transfer time, verify all three dates and cities under one itinerary for one traveler, compare the complete fare conditions, and book the flights.
events.scenario_brief: The Washington museum confirms that Avery can leave by 3:30 p.m. Wednesday, and the exhibition cases will travel by contracted truck rather than with her. Two Washington-to-Boston flights now provide realistic airport transfer margins, while the previously identified Monday outbound and Friday return remain available.

events.continuity_hook: Confirmed arrival and departure times now determine both hotel stays and expose different cost and access tradeoffs in each city.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate complete totals for both two-night stays, compare travel times to each museum and the cancellation terms, and reserve one suitable hotel in Washington and one in Boston.
events.scenario_brief: The multi-city flights are booked, leaving Avery to arrange two nights in Washington and two in Boston. In Washington, the closest property is convenient for the Tuesday review but charges a destination fee; in Boston, one option is walkable to Friday's receiving meeting while another requires a short transit ride and has a materially later cancellation deadline.

events.continuity_hook: The three flights and both hotel stays were already reserved, but the later Boston meeting requires adjustment of only the final air segment.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the later Friday flights against the new meeting end time and airport transfer, move the Boston-to-Atlanta segment, confirm the fare difference, and verify that neither hotel reservation needs altered dates.
events.scenario_brief: Four days before Avery's Atlanta-Washington-Boston work trip, the Boston museum moves Friday's receiving meeting from the morning to 2:00 p.m. Her booked Boston-to-Atlanta flight now leaves too early, while the Washington and Boston hotel stays remain correctly dated; two later Friday returns are available at different fare differences.

events.continuity_hook: This opens their longer annual coastal trip after the recent sequence of work and family travel.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the two destinations for the fixed week, identify available beachfront or near-beach properties, and retain a manageable set of lodging options with complete seven-night totals.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife begin planning a seven-night September coastal vacation within driving distance of Atlanta. They are considering St. Simons Island and Hilton Head Island, and need one room for two adults; direct beach access, the complete stay cost, and availability for their fixed Saturday-to-Saturday week remain unresolved.

events.continuity_hook: The destination decision narrows the open coastal search to one island and three realistic properties for the same seven-night stay.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate the full cost of each property, verify the actual walk or access route to the beach, compare cancellation terms, and reduce the choice to one or two hotels.
events.scenario_brief: After reviewing both destinations, Avery and her wife choose St. Simons Island. Three available properties remain: one directly on the beach, one across a road from public beach access, and one several blocks inland with a lower total; resort fees, parking charges, and cancellation deadlines differ.

events.continuity_hook: The prior cost and access comparison left two hotels, but room category details and current inventory now determine the practical choice.
events.interaction_goal: Verify room layouts and view descriptions for two adults, compare the exact totals of the viable room categories, confirm current availability, and select the hotel and room to book.
events.scenario_brief: The beachfront hotel and the property across from public access are the finalists. At the beachfront hotel, the least expensive room faces the parking area while a higher category has a balcony and partial ocean view; the other property offers a larger room but requires crossing a busy road, and availability has tightened for the fixed week.

events.continuity_hook: The hotel and room category are settled, leaving only the rate terms and complete charge to confirm.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the seven nights, two-adult occupancy, full price breakdown, payment schedule, and cancellation deadline, then reserve the selected balcony room and verify the confirmation details.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife select the beachfront hotel's balcony room for their Saturday-to-Saturday stay. The room is still available, but the refundable and prepaid rates have different totals and payment timing, and the quoted amount must be reconciled with taxes, the daily resort fee, and parking before purchase.

events.continuity_hook: The confirmed coastal reservation is affected by construction shortly before arrival, creating a choice between changing rooms during the stay and accepting a different full-stay category.
events.interaction_goal: Clarify the location and features of the offered full-stay room, compare it with the two-room arrangement, choose how to handle the construction issue, and obtain an updated written confirmation with the same dates and total.
events.scenario_brief: Ten days before the coastal vacation, the hotel advises that balcony repairs may affect Avery and her wife's reserved room category during the first two nights. It offers either a temporary standard room followed by a move, a partial-ocean-view room for the full stay at no added charge, or cancellation without penalty; beach access and the original stay dates are unchanged.

events.continuity_hook: The coastal stay is complete, but the final folio does not match the written terms issued after the balcony-room construction issue.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the reservation, updated room terms, and final folio; identify the unexplained adjustment; and obtain a corrected charge and itemized receipt.
events.scenario_brief: After returning from St. Simons Island, Avery reviews the emailed hotel folio and finds a room-category adjustment applied to the first two nights even though the construction accommodation was promised at the original total. The stay dates, resort fees, and parking charges otherwise match the reservation.

events.continuity_hook: This opens a new work trip with a fixed arrival requirement and an uncertain return window.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Sunday outbound flights that allow a settled arrival before Monday's inspection, map Thursday return options around the possible signoff times, and retain a workable round trip without purchasing the uncertain return yet.
events.scenario_brief: Avery is assigned to oversee a lender installation in Philadelphia, with a Monday morning mount inspection and a Thursday lender signoff. She needs to travel from Atlanta on Sunday and return Thursday, but the signoff's end time has not been finalized and the exhibition components will move separately by truck.

events.continuity_hook: The confirmed signoff window resolves the only schedule uncertainty in the proposed work itinerary.
events.interaction_goal: Recheck the Sunday departure, compare the two feasible Thursday returns by total fare and timing, select the complete itinerary for one traveler, and book it.
events.scenario_brief: The Philadelphia lender confirms that Thursday's signoff should finish by noon. The Sunday outbound previously identified remains available, and two Thursday nonstop returns provide realistic airport-transfer margins, with the later flight costing less but arriving in Atlanta near midnight.

events.continuity_hook: Confirmed flight times now fix the lodging dates and allow the Philadelphia work trip to be completed.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate the full four-night cost of both hotels, verify the Monday morning route to the museum and each cancellation deadline, and reserve one room for Avery.
events.scenario_brief: With the Sunday-to-Thursday flights booked, Avery needs four hotel nights in Philadelphia. One property is a short walk from the museum but has a mandatory nightly fee, while another has a lower complete total and requires a direct transit ride; their cancellation deadlines also differ.

events.continuity_hook: This begins a shared family visit with fixed weekend dates but unresolved outbound timing and Sunday plans.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Friday evening and Sunday round-trip combinations for two travelers, check complete fares and practical arrival times, and retain options for both possible Sunday schedules.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife plan a Friday-to-Sunday trip from Atlanta to Nashville for a Saturday evening family anniversary dinner. They need flights for two adults, cannot leave until after work on Friday, and are weighing an early Sunday return against a later flight that leaves time for a family brunch.

events.continuity_hook: The Sunday commitment settles the flight choice, while the overnight arrangements add a hotel decision before the family trip can be booked.
events.interaction_goal: Book the selected Friday evening and Sunday afternoon flights for two adults, compare both hotels by full two-night total and travel time to the dinner and brunch, and reserve one shared room.
events.scenario_brief: The family brunch is confirmed for late Sunday morning, so Avery and her wife can choose the later return flight. Their relatives cannot host overnight, leaving them to select one room for two nights between a hotel near the anniversary venue and a less expensive property closer to the airport.

events.continuity_hook: The flights and shared hotel were booked after the brunch time was settled, but the schedule change reopens only the return leg of the Nashville family visit.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the airline's change options for both travelers, compare the evening nonstop with the midafternoon connecting itinerary by added cost and Atlanta arrival, and reissue the return without altering the Friday outbound.
events.scenario_brief: The airline moves Avery and her wife's booked Sunday return from midafternoon to shortly before noon, which now overlaps the family brunch. An evening nonstop is available with a fare difference, while a midafternoon one-stop itinerary would preserve more of the original arrival time but add a connection.

events.continuity_hook: This begins a new museum work trip after the Nashville family visit is resolved, with a fixed arrival day and an unsettled return window.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Monday flights that provide a reasonable margin before Tuesday's crate opening, identify Thursday evening and Friday morning return possibilities, and hold off on selecting the return until the lender inspection time is confirmed.
events.scenario_brief: Avery is assigned to a collection installation in Kansas City with a Tuesday morning crate opening, Wednesday installation work, and a Thursday lender inspection whose finish time is still provisional. She must leave Atlanta on Monday, and the art shipment will travel separately through the museum's carrier.

events.continuity_hook: The confirmed inspection schedule resolves the timing question left open during the first Kansas City flight search.
events.interaction_goal: Recheck the Monday flight, compare the two feasible Thursday returns by transfer margin, elapsed travel time, and complete fare, then book the round trip for Avery.
events.scenario_brief: The lender sets Thursday's inspection for 1:00 p.m. and expects it to end by 3:00 p.m. The preferred Monday outbound remains available, and two Thursday returns are feasible: an early-evening nonstop with a tighter airport transfer and a later one-stop itinerary with a longer travel day.

events.continuity_hook: The completed flight itinerary fixes the hotel dates and narrows the remaining work-trip planning to lodging for one traveler.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate each hotel's full three-night total, verify the Tuesday morning route to the museum and the exact cancellation terms, and reserve one room through Thursday checkout.
events.scenario_brief: With Monday and Thursday flights booked, Avery needs three nights in Kansas City. A hotel within walking distance of the museum charges a destination fee and has a Wednesday cancellation deadline, while a lower-priced property requires a short rideshare and becomes nonrefundable several days earlier.

events.continuity_hook: The Kansas City trip was fully booked, but the canceled return creates linked flight, work-approval, and lodging decisions shortly before departure.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the three rerouting paths by arrival time, connection risk, ground-transfer burden, and added hotel cost; verify the airline's rebooking terms; and preserve the best Thursday and Friday options while Avery seeks approval for an extra night.
events.scenario_brief: Two days before Avery's scheduled return, the airline cancels her Thursday nonstop. The remaining Thursday choices are a late one-stop flight with a short connection or an evening departure to a nearby airport followed by a long ground transfer; a Friday morning nonstop is also available, and her hotel can extend the room for one night at a different rate.

events.continuity_hook: The approval and extended museum duty settle the choice among the alternatives identified after the canceled Thursday flight.
events.interaction_goal: Rebook Avery onto the Friday nonstop, extend the same hotel room by one night, confirm any fare or room-rate difference, and verify the updated departure, checkout, and confirmation details.
events.scenario_brief: Avery's museum approves the extra night because the lender also asks her to remain through Thursday evening pack-out. The Friday morning nonstop and the additional night at her current hotel are still available, but both confirmations need to align with the revised checkout and airport-transfer timing.

events.continuity_hook: The Kansas City installation trip is complete, allowing Avery to turn to the couple's longer coastal vacation for the year.
events.interaction_goal: Compare viable flight schedules and well-rated coastal lodging in both destinations, estimate the combined transportation and eight-night room totals, and identify which island offers the stronger practical itinerary for the fixed dates.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife begin planning an eight-night late-May coastal vacation and are choosing between San Juan and St. Thomas. Their dates are fixed from Saturday through the following Sunday, they need round-trip travel from Atlanta for two adults and one shared room, and they want to compare actual beach access, recent guest ratings, and complete trip costs before committing to either island.

events.continuity_hook: Selecting St. Thomas narrows the open vacation planning to a specific round trip and lodging search.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the complete round-trip fares for two adults, elapsed travel times, connection details, and usable time on the island, then retain the best nonstop and connecting combinations while Avery confirms one remaining work commitment.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife choose St. Thomas after reviewing the two destination estimates. For the Saturday outbound, they can take an early nonstop or a less expensive one-stop trip arriving late in the afternoon; the Sunday return choices include a midday nonstop and an evening connecting itinerary that preserves more vacation time but reaches Atlanta much later.

events.continuity_hook: The cleared work commitment removes the only obstacle to choosing the faster outbound identified in the flight comparison.
events.interaction_goal: Recheck the selected nonstop flights, confirm the full fare and baggage charges for both travelers, choose available adjacent seats including Avery's window seat, and book the round trip.
events.scenario_brief: Avery's exhibition calendar is cleared for the Friday before departure, so the early Saturday nonstop is now practical. The preferred Sunday midday nonstop remains available, and Avery and her wife want adjacent seats, with a window seat for Avery, before the fare changes.

events.continuity_hook: Confirmed arrival and departure times now fix the exact lodging dates for the couple's stay.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate the complete eight-night totals for the realistic room and rate combinations, compare beach access and transportation needs, inspect recent ratings, and identify a refundable first choice plus a viable alternate.
events.scenario_brief: With the flights booked, Avery and her wife need one room for eight nights in St. Thomas. A beachfront resort offers direct sand access but adds mandatory daily resort and parking charges, while a highly rated hillside property has a lower room total, no direct beach access, and scheduled transport to two beaches; refundable and advance-purchase rates are available at each.

events.continuity_hook: The loss of the original room reopens the lodging choice without affecting the already booked flights or vacation dates.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the ocean-view resort room with the condo-style hotel by full cost, deposit schedule, cancellation deadline, beach access, and recent ratings, then reserve one room for both travelers for all eight nights.
events.scenario_brief: The standard room at the preferred beachfront resort sells out before Avery books it. An ocean-view room there is still available at a higher total, while a newly available condo-style hotel has direct beach access, a kitchenette, and a lower complete price but requires a larger deposit and has an earlier cancellation deadline.

events.continuity_hook: The coastal vacation is fully booked, but the airline schedule change and incomplete arrival record require a coordinated follow-up before travel.
events.interaction_goal: Compare accepting the earlier nonstop with moving to the evening connection, verify the resulting checkout and airport-transfer timing, confirm the selected flight arrangement for both travelers, and add the outbound arrival details to the hotel reservation.
events.scenario_brief: The airline moves the booked Sunday nonstop ninety minutes earlier, leaving less time between hotel checkout and departure but still allowing a normal airport transfer. Avery and her wife can accept the new time at no charge or move to an evening one-stop itinerary; their hotel also needs the arrival time entered on the reservation so it can hold the room for their Saturday check-in.

events.continuity_hook: The couple already accepted the airline's earlier Sunday nonstop and added their Saturday arrival time to the reservation; the hotel's access notice creates the remaining pre-trip decision.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the duration and location of the path closure, compare the two units' beach routes, view, deposit timing, and Saturday check-in arrangements, and place the ocean-view unit on hold while the couple decides.
events.scenario_brief: Ten days before departure, the condo-style hotel advises Avery and her wife that resurfacing work will close the shortest path to the beach during the first two days of their eight-night stay. They can keep the booked studio and use a longer marked route, or move at no added room charge to an ocean-view unit with a balcony in another building, though the replacement unit has a different deposit schedule and later check-in time.

events.continuity_hook: The hotel's answers resolve the tradeoffs identified after the beach-path closure notice.
events.interaction_goal: Move the reservation to the held ocean-view unit, confirm luggage storage and the new balance due date, and check that both travelers, all eight nights, and the flight arrival information remain on the confirmation.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife decide that the later check-in is manageable because the hotel can store their luggage after the morning flight arrives. The held ocean-view unit remains available, and the hotel has confirmed in writing that the room rate and eight-night total will not increase, although the balance will now be collected at check-in rather than before arrival.

events.continuity_hook: The annual coastal trip is complete, and a newly assigned exhibition installation begins the next work-travel episode.
events.interaction_goal: Map viable Wednesday outbound and Friday return flights, compare two-night lodging near the lender and gallery, estimate complete airfare and hotel costs, and identify any schedule details Avery must confirm before booking.
events.scenario_brief: After returning from St. Thomas, Avery is assigned a mid-June trip from Atlanta to Providence for a lender condition check on Thursday morning and a gallery installation scheduled through 4:00 p.m. Friday. She expects to travel Wednesday and return Friday evening, but needs to determine whether same-day return flights leave enough time to reach the airport and whether a downtown hotel or an airport-area property is more practical for the two work sites.

events.continuity_hook: The confirmed Wednesday handoff resolves the outbound timing left open in the initial Providence search while the Friday return still requires a risk and cost comparison.
events.interaction_goal: Recheck the morning outbound, compare the Friday options by total fare, airport-transfer margin, elapsed time, and connection details, then book the best round trip for Avery.
events.scenario_brief: The lender confirms that Avery must report to its receiving dock by 3:30 p.m. Wednesday for a crate handoff, making the morning nonstop the practical outbound. Two Friday returns remain possible after the scheduled installation: a nonstop with a workable but limited transfer window and a lower-fare one-stop itinerary departing later and arriving in Atlanta near midnight.

events.continuity_hook: The confirmed flight times fix Avery's check-in and checkout dates and remove airfare from the remaining Providence arrangements.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate both complete two-night totals, verify the routes to the lender and gallery and the airport transfer after Friday's installation, and reserve one room through Friday checkout.
events.scenario_brief: With the Wednesday morning and Friday evening flights booked, Avery needs two hotel nights. A downtown property is walkable to Thursday's lender appointment and a short ride from Friday's gallery, while a less expensive airport hotel includes a shuttle but would require longer ground trips both workdays; each has a different tax-inclusive total and cancellation deadline.

events.continuity_hook: The Providence flights and hotel were complete until the installation schedule expanded beyond the transfer margin used for the original Friday booking.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the later Friday itinerary with the Saturday nonstop by sign-off margin, arrival time, connection risk, fare difference, and extra lodging cost; verify the airline's change terms and the hotel's one-night extension terms; and hold the practical options while Avery obtains authorization.
events.scenario_brief: Four days before departure, the gallery moves final lighting and the lender sign-off to Friday evening, so Avery can no longer reach her booked return flight. A later one-stop flight could still get her home Friday night if the sign-off ends on time, while a Saturday morning nonstop would require extending her current hotel by one night at a higher rate.

events.continuity_hook: The authorization resolves the cost question left open when Friday's work schedule moved beyond Avery's booked departure.
events.interaction_goal: Replace the unusable Friday return with the Saturday morning nonstop, confirm the fare difference and application of the original ticket value, extend the same hotel room through Saturday checkout, and obtain updated confirmations before both holds expire.
events.scenario_brief: Avery receives approval to stay through Saturday, removing the risk of relying on the tight Friday-night connection after the lender sign-off. The Saturday morning nonstop and the additional night at her current downtown hotel are still available, but both holds expire that afternoon and the airline credit from the original return must be applied correctly.

events.continuity_hook: The Providence installation is complete, and the Chicago loan movement begins a separate work trip with fixed museum appointments but unresolved travel dates and lodging location.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Monday and Tuesday outbound flights against the loan-delivery deadline, identify viable Thursday returns after the briefing, calculate complete airfare and two- or three-night hotel totals, and determine which schedule should be submitted for approval.
events.scenario_brief: Avery is assigned to accompany a loan from Atlanta to Chicago for a Tuesday afternoon delivery, remain for a Wednesday condition review, and attend a Thursday morning installation briefing. She can fly Monday afternoon or early Tuesday, and the return cannot leave until Thursday after the briefing; lodging near the museum is convenient for the work schedule, while properties near the airport reduce the final transfer but add substantial commuting on Tuesday and Wednesday.

events.continuity_hook: The confirmed truck meeting resolves the outbound-date question from the first Chicago search while leaving the return timing and cost to be settled.
events.interaction_goal: Recheck the Monday nonstop, compare the Thursday returns by fare, travel time, and transfer margin from the museum, then book the practical round trip for Avery and record the ticket terms needed for the work authorization.
events.scenario_brief: The registrar confirms that Avery must meet the loan truck at the Chicago museum by 10:30 a.m. Tuesday, making the early Tuesday flight too vulnerable to a delay. A Monday afternoon nonstop now fits the handoff plan, while two Thursday returns remain feasible after the installation briefing: an earlier nonstop with a modest airport-transfer margin and a later nonstop at a higher fare.

versions.boundary_condition: Treat this as a preference rather than an absolute requirement unless the user explicitly says no layovers for the current trip.
versions.condition: When searching for outbound or return flights, prioritize nonstop options.
versions.default_action: Search for and present a nonstop itinerary first.
versions.exception_condition: If no suitable nonstop flight is available, a one-stop option may be acceptable, but confirm the tradeoff before booking.
versions.name: Prefer nonstop flights
versions.scope_condition: Recurring domestic museum work trips where fixed access windows make itinerary simplicity valuable.

versions.boundary_condition: Treat the preference as a flexible later-day window ranging from afternoon to after 6:00 p.m., not as a fixed cutoff
versions.condition: When selecting a return flight and multiple departure times are available
versions.default_action: Prioritize return options departing in the afternoon or evening
versions.exception_condition: Use another departure period when the traveler explicitly requests it for the current trip or no later-day option is workable
versions.name: Prefer later-day return flights
versions.scope_condition: Return legs from museum work trips when the final day's duties end early enough to allow a later departure.

versions.boundary_condition: This is a soft preference: the evidence supports Delta as a favored option, not as the only acceptable airline or an always-first choice over every other preferred carrier.
versions.condition: When choosing among flight carriers and Delta is available while also satisfying the trip's schedule, route, price, and stop constraints.
versions.default_action: Search for or present Delta options as part of the preferred carrier set, and favor Delta when it is otherwise comparable to alternatives.
versions.exception_condition: Use another acceptable carrier when Delta is unavailable, materially worse, or does not meet the current trip constraints.
versions.name: Delta as a soft preferred carrier option
versions.preference_value: Delta is a preferred airline to include in the flight shortlist, but not an exclusive carrier requirement.
versions.scope_condition: Commercial flights originating from or returning to her Atlanta home base when multiple carriers satisfy the trip constraints.

versions.boundary_condition: Applies only to seat location. If seat selection is unavailable at booking or is deferred until check-in, note that limitation and try to secure a window seat at the earliest available time.
versions.condition: When booking or selecting seats for flights where a seat location preference can be applied.
versions.default_action: Prefer or request a window seat by default.
versions.exception_condition: Use a different seat only if the user specifies another seat preference, needs a different seating arrangement, or no acceptable window seat is available.
versions.name: prefers_window_seat_on_flights
versions.scope_condition: Seat selection for her recurring solo work flights and occasional personal flights when seat choice is available.

versions.boundary_condition: Apply this per room and do not infer it from the number of travelers or requested rooms.
versions.condition: When selecting a shared hotel room without an explicit request for separate beds.
versions.default_action: Prefer a room with a queen-size bed; a king-size bed may be accepted when offered as a larger alternative.
versions.exception_condition: Honor explicit twin-bed, separate-bed, or other room-specific sleeping arrangements instead.
versions.name: queen_bed_for_shared_hotel_room
versions.preference_value: Prefer a queen-size bed for a shared hotel room when no separate-bed arrangement is requested.
versions.scope_condition: Personal trips where Avery and her wife book one shared hotel room and have not requested separate beds.

versions.boundary_condition: Treat walking distance as the reusable threshold; use a stricter walk-time limit only when the current request explicitly supplies one
versions.condition: When searching for a hotel in a coastal or beach-oriented area
versions.default_action: Prioritize properties on the beach or close enough to walk while also filtering to the trip's stated budget
versions.exception_condition: Do not apply this preference to non-coastal trips or when the current trip names a different location priority
versions.name: Prefer beach-proximate hotels
versions.preference_value: A hotel on or near the beach, ideally within walking distance
versions.scope_condition: The couple's recurring beach-oriented vacation when comparing hotels within the stated trip budget.

versions.boundary_condition: Use a 3.5 minimum when the search is explicitly budget-focused. Apply either threshold only to the rating metric under discussion, and do not conflate hotel class, Google ratings, and customer-review ratings.
versions.condition: When a hotel search calls for a well-rated property and frames the stay as nice, upscale, resort-style, or explicitly budget-focused.
versions.default_action: Filter or prioritize options meeting a 4.0 minimum for nice, upscale, or resort-style searches, and identify the rating source when known.
versions.exception_condition: Follow any newly stated threshold or metric. If no suitable option meets the applicable floor while satisfying more important trip constraints, ask before relaxing it.
versions.name: contextual_hotel_rating_floor
versions.preference_value: Prefer hotels rated at least 4.0 when seeking a nice, upscale, or resort-style stay; for explicitly budget-focused searches, prefer at least 3.5.
versions.scope_condition: Annual coastal leisure searches framed as a nice, upscale, or resort-style stay, and any explicitly budget-focused variant of that search.
